item.text:
## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix `finished_at` before merge because it reports a start time as a completion time.

## Changes

The pull request adds a conditional `finished_at` column to the current-state model, documents it in the schema catalog, and retains one row per process based on its latest event.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Align `finished_at` with the event it records — Process 20 has only a `started` event, yet `finished_at` returns that event’s `occurred_at` as the completion time. The source schema at `sources/process_events.sql:4` defines no completion event. — Consumers that treat a populated `finished_at` as evidence of completion can classify newly started processes as finished. — Fix: Use `started_at` for the start timestamp, or define a completion event and populate `finished_at` from it.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Document when the timestamp is `NULL` — Process 30 has a `started` event followed by `cleared`, yet its timestamp is `NULL`. “NULL means the process has never been started” contradicts `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end`, which evaluates only the latest event. — Consumers filtering for never-started processes by `NULL` will also select previously started processes whose latest event is `cleared`.

## Suggestions

- models/schema.yml:12 — comments — Document that the source offset is preserved — A latest `started` event with `occurred_at = '2026-01-01T01:00:00+01:00' retains its offset. “Stored in UTC using the source event timestamp” contradicts `then occurred_at`, which returns the source text unchanged. — Consumers sorting the timestamp as UTC text can get the wrong chronological order when source offsets vary.
- models/processes.sql:10 — tests — Assert a null timestamp for a created-only process — No test asserts the `NULL` result for a process whose only event is `created`. The source data includes this input as process 10 without checking the model output. — A regression that populates the timestamp before a process starts would go undetected for this input.
